summary.name: How release canaries can save your bacon
summary.one_liner: A Google Cloud Blog article by Google SRE Adrian Hilton explaining how to use release canarying, staged rollouts and automated analysis to detect bad software releases early.
use_cases: planning a safe production software rollout
deciding percentage steps for a gradual release
setting up canary monitoring and alerts
versioning cached JavaScript for quick web rollbacks
summary.what_it_does: The article describes canarying as sending a new binary or configuration to a small first instance that receives live production traffic, then monitoring it for errors, latency and load before a wider release. It argues manual graph inspection is unreliable and describes Google's automated canary analysis that rolls back automatically. It covers client canarying for Android (Play Store staged rollouts) and web clients (versioned JavaScript), and gives example rollout step sequences such as 1%, 10%, 100% for internal binaries and 10%, 50%, 100% for Android apps. It is an essay, not a software tool.
notable: Describes Google's automated canary analysis that detects elevated errors, latency and load and rolls back automatically
Gives concrete release percentage step examples and advice on wait times between steps
Covers client canarying for Android Play Store staged rollouts and versioned JavaScript for web clients
caveats: Describes Google's internal practices; it is not a downloadable tool
Play Store staged rollouts give little control over when users update or whether they accept updates
Automated rollback only works if rollbacks are safe
